preamble: Insertion of a palatal glide [j], typically before word-initial front vowels (prothesis) or in hiatus. Slavic languages regularly show a prothetic j- before inherited initial *e- (Proto-Slavic *esmь 'I am' > Old Church Slavonic ѥсмь jesmĭ), and Romanian pronounces initial e- in personal pronouns and forms of 'to be' with [j] (el [jel] 'he').

examples.to: OCS ѥсмь (jesmĭ), Russian есмь (jesmʹ), Old Polish jeśm
examples.note: Word-initial *e- acquired a prothetic [j] in the Slavic languages; compare the Baltic cognate Lithuanian esmì without it.
Romanian inserts [j] before initial e- in personal pronouns and forms of the verb 'to be', a glide absent from the Latin source forms.
